basis: Tuberculosis is a mycobacterial infection predominantly located in the lungs; rifampicin resistance does not establish additional organ involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the predominant site of tuberculosis; antimicrobial resistance does not change its usual anatomical classification.

basis: Reticular extraneural perineurioma occupies dermal or subcutaneous soft tissue; involvement of a peripheral nerve is not defining.

decisions.neurologic: none: extraneural perineurial differentiation does not establish origin within, occupation of, or damage to a peripheral nerve.

basis: Direct neurotoxicity, acute kidney injury and interstitial pneumonitis are documented at 30-79%; blood-pressure changes alone do not establish lasting cardiovascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension is annotated at 30-79%, but the evidence does not distinguish transient toxic blood-pressure changes from persistent cardiovascular disease.

basis: Progressive skeletal-muscle dystrophy; dysphagia in 12/32 reflects muscle dysfunction without demonstrated gastrointestinal injury. Respiratory muscle weakness occurs in 3/32.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia in 12/32 (~38%) reflects dystrophic swallowing muscles; separate damage to gastrointestinal tissue is not established.

basis: Neurologic dysfunction ~70%; optic atrophy 17/31; sensorineural hearing loss 30-79%. Alopecia/skin disease ~70-77% omitted at cap in favor of severe sensory injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none at cap: alopecia affects 24/31 and rash 21/31; irreversible neurologic, visual and auditory injury take priority.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 30-79% and may persist despite treatment; retained for its severity.

basis: Brain malformations and hydrocephalus occur in 13/13. Polydactyly is an explicitly defining skeletal feature despite occurring in only 2/13.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is explicitly included in the syndrome's name and definition; the 30% threshold applies to involved organs, not defining primary features.

basis: Adrenal medullary endocrine tumor; secondary hypertension is a separately diagnosed disease. Direct myocardial injury affects fewer than 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (~80-90%) is a separately diagnosed secondary disease; catecholamine cardiomyopathy affects a minority below 30%.

basis: Defining T-cell dysfunction and autoimmune hemolysis; hepatic failure/cholestasis and cardiomyopathy each 1/3. Atrophic gastritis (1/3) omitted at cap; cohort is small.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defective T-cell function and predominant autoimmune hemolytic anemia are part of the disease's own definition.

basis: Cowden mucocutaneous hamartomas include defining oral papillomas. Benign thyroid nodules/goiter affect ~50-75% in Cowden disease; SDHD-specific frequency is uncertain.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral papillomatosis is a defining Cowden mucocutaneous manifestation; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: benign thyroid nodules/goiter commonly affect ~50-75% in the parent Cowden phenotype; this reflects existing lesions, not cancer risk alone.

basis: Classic Zellweger disease has defining metabolic, cerebral and hepatic disease; renal cystic dysplasia occurs in >30%. Epiphyseal stippling (1/1) and sensory disease omitted at cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: congenital hepatic disease is a defining component of classic Zellweger syndrome; hepatomegaly is recorded in 1/1.
decisions.renal: involved: renal cortical cystic dysplasia is common (>30%) in classic Zellweger disease and represents direct structural involvement.
decisions.neurologic: primary: congenital brain abnormalities and profound neonatal neurologic dysfunction define classic Zellweger disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: epiphyseal stippling is documented in 1/1, but cerebral, hepatic and renal disease take priority for their greater functional severity.
